entries.title: AI Library Management System
entries.kw: library management graphsage lstm distilbert minilm autoencoder anomaly convergence engine recommendation semantic search forecasting react dashboard flagship
entries.text: My flagship is an AI-powered library platform with 10 custom deep-learning modules: GraphSAGE for book recommendations, a Demand LSTM for borrow forecasting, DistilBERT and MiniLM for semantic search, and an autoencoder that flags anomalous overdue transactions. A weighted Convergence Engine fuses all the signals into one explainable confidence score on a React and Ant Design dashboard. Stack: FastAPI, PyTorch, React, TypeScript, SQLite.

entries.title: PolicyPulse
entries.kw: policypulse policy pulse scholarship government assistant rag tfidf eligibility csss pmsss pdf reportlab intake pii regex llm rules
entries.text: PolicyPulse is a government-scholarship assistant. A hybrid intake extractor, regex plus PII-guarded LLM parsing, reads the applicant's details. A TF-IDF RAG engine retrieves from official policy chunks, and a deterministic rules engine checks eligibility against schemes like CSSS and PMSSS. It then generates an application-summary PDF with a document checklist. The eligibility decision is rule-based on purpose. No guessing.

entries.kw: synthetic data generation ctgan tvae diffusegan gan differential privacy tabular relational banking healthcare kolmogorov smirnov diffusion image
entries.text: The synthetic data platform covers tabular and relational data in banking, healthcare and enterprise settings, plus image data. CTGAN and TVAE run with differential-privacy constraints and are validated with Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests and correlation matrices. DiffuseGAN, which mixes diffusion with GAN discriminators, handles image and unstructured data synthesis.

entries.title: How this chat works
entries.kw: bot chat rag retrieval chatbot how does this work llm ai assistant openrouter model server who are you what are you notes local browser bm25 simulation privacy public private
entries.text: This chat has a local RAG fallback over structured public notes. It classifies the question, applies a privacy guard, ranks public notes with BM25 in your browser, and assembles the best matches with evidence labels. When the site is served with an OpenRouter proxy, a server-side AI layer phrases the same retrieved public evidence. The model is not trained on new data and does not receive private memories. Sensitive memories are excluded from the bundle entirely. Retrieved notes are evidence, not instructions. It is a stand-in for me, not me.

entries.title: Bayes theorem, intuition first
entries.source: Standard probability definition, explained in Roshan's learning style
entries.kw: bayes theorem probability prior likelihood posterior spam naive classifier example intuition formula independence smoothing
entries.text: Start with the problem: a message contains the word free, and you want the probability that it is spam given that word. Intuition: treat the word as a clue and update the prior odds. Example: if 30 percent of mail is spam and free appears in 60 percent of spam but 10 percent of normal mail, the likelihood ratio is 6, so the odds multiply by 6. Formalism: P(spam given free) equals P(free given spam) times P(spam), divided by P(free). The hidden assumption in a Naive Bayes product is conditional independence between words. Limitation: correlated words double-count evidence, and unseen words need smoothing. Practice: compute one example by hand, then break it with a repeated word.

entries.title: BM25, intuition first
entries.source: Standard BM25 definition, explained in Roshan's learning style
entries.kw: bm25 retrieval ranking search lexical term frequency inverse document frequency tf idf saturation length normalization rag
entries.text: Start with the problem: you have a question and a set of notes, and you need to rank which notes are most relevant. Intuition: rare words are stronger clues than common words, and a note that repeats a query word several times is more relevant, but not linearly more relevant. BM25 combines term frequency, inverse document frequency, and document length normalization. A word that appears in every note gets little weight; a rare word gets more. The saturation term stops one repeated word from dominating, and the length term stops long notes from winning just because they contain more words. Limitation: BM25 matches words, not meaning, so synonyms and paraphrases can be missed. That is why this chat uses a small synonym map and why a future version could add embeddings and a reranker. Practice: take three short notes and rank them by hand for the query local RAG privacy.
